newsitem.title: JAPAN: New Japan virtual pet hatches offsprings.
newsitem.headline: New Japan virtual pet hatches offsprings.

text.p: Japan's popular electronic "virtual pet" will soon be able to mate with other electronic pets and hatch offspring, the Tokyo Shimbun said on Saturday.

The latest generation of the "Tamagotchi", an electronic chicken-like figure on a liquid crystal display which is fed and cleaned by pressing buttons, will be rolled out by Japanese toymaker Bandai Company Ltd in August.
The latest models will be either male or female. After being reared to adulthood, they can then "mate" with other Tamagotchi of the opposite sex and hatch offspring, the daily said.
The parent eventually disappears after caring for the younger one, a process which continues from generation to generation.
The "virtual pets" are proving highly popular in Japan where crowded living conditions can make owning a real pet difficult.
"Tamagotchi", or lovable egg, begins life as a bird-like image on the screen of an egg-shaped keyring device. It develops from a chick to an adult in around 10 days.
But the owner must feed, groom and soothe the digital creature or it will waste away and die from neglect.
Nearly 1.5 million "Tamagotchi" have sold since November.
Earlier this month, Bandai said that in May and June it would start selling angel fish and forest animal variations of the original Tamogotchi.
